title: Switch Transformer: Scaling to Trillion-Parameter Models
hook: Route every token to exactly one expert instead of many - this single simplification made trillion-parameter MoE models stable enough to train at scale.
key_points: Replaces top-k expert routing with top-1 ('switch') routing, cutting communication and gating complexity.
Demonstrates models with up to a trillion parameters trained on TPUs while keeping per-token FLOPs roughly constant.
Introduces auxiliary load-balancing losses to prevent routing collapse where one expert dominates.
Achieves 7x faster pre-training than a dense T5 baseline at the same compute budget.
content_html: Fedus, Zoph, and Shazeer at Google Brain showed in 2021 that simplifying MoE routing to a single expert per token - the "switch" - removed enough complexity to make trillion-parameter Transformer models trainable. The paper appeared on arXiv in January 2021.
extra_html:
How it works

Each Switch layer replaces the dense feed-forward block in a standard Transformer with a set of expert feed-forward networks. A router sends each token to exactly one expert (top-1), rather than blending outputs from several. A learned auxiliary loss penalizes uneven routing so that no single expert becomes a bottleneck. Expert capacity buffers are used to handle overflow when too many tokens land on one expert in the same batch.

Why it matters

The Switch Transformer showed that sparse MoE Transformers can train faster per FLOP than dense models of comparable quality, opening the door to trillion-parameter scale without proportionally larger compute budgets. The 7x pre-training speedup over T5 made the design hard to ignore. Read the full paper on arXiv for training recipes, stability tricks, and ablations across model sizes.
